## W. David Walter
My current role as Professor of Disease Ecology is in the Department of Veterinary Microbiology and Pathology at Washington State University as of September 2026. My research focuses on investigations of the treponeme-associated hoof disease (TAHD) in elk populations in the state of Washington. In addition to research on wild elk populations infected with TAHD, I am responsible for a small, captive elk facility on campus. The captive facility has been used to investigate transmission of TAHD to naive elk and impacts of the disease on individual elk.

Previously (2011-2026), I was the Assistant Unit Leader at the Pennsylvania Cooperative Fish and Wildlife Research Unit (Unit) and serve as Adjunct Associate Professor of Wildlife Ecology in the Department of Ecosystem Science and Management (Department) at The Pennsylvania State University (PSU).
